assumptions: The product is an exception-control layer that complements rather than replaces ECHA preparation, validation, and submission tooling.
Exact formula data remains inside each end customer's controlled environment, while the entrant centralizes only non-confidential rules and compatibility tests.
Qualified consultants retain regulatory judgment, and each end customer remains the legal duty holder and controls submission identity.
The founder uses no employer data, systems, vendors, work time, or intellectual property and obtains explicit conflict clearance before any production engagement.
Consultant adoption, deployment acceptance, pricing, usage volume, support cost, retention, and the stated margin are hypotheses because the bound research contains no customer or channel validation.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Mandatory PCN maintenance, one-composition UFI discipline, and recurring formula, label, language, and market changes create a credible need for cross-record exception control. Positioning the product above free submission tools and keeping formulas customer-controlled is coherent, but the research does not establish that reconciliation is a costly, frequent bottleneck for the proposed consultant segment.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: The compliance obligation and documented enforcement gap support consequential pain, and recurring updates can make errors expensive. However, the 19% non-notification rate does not establish budget or outsourcing demand, and there is no evidence that consultants will pay, trust the deployment model, or prefer automation that might compress their billable work.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Implementation, annual-license, and usage revenue could create attractive recurring economics if one consultant carries the product across many client releases. The proposed prices, 55% EBITDA, 45-practice scale, payback, retention, and 7-9 year founder-value path are unsupported, while customer-specific integration, security review, annual format regression, support, and insurance could prevent software-like margins.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Independent SDS/CLP consultancies handling repeated hazardous-mixture releases form a specific, operationally coherent beachhead and could aggregate SME demand. Its economic depth is unknown: the research does not quantify qualifying practices, client portfolios, release frequency, current spend, or the share poorly served by free and incumbent tools.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A privacy-preserving, consultant-operated exception queue may occupy a narrower position than broad enterprise product-compliance suites. Yet ECHA already supplies free preparation, validation, multimarket, and system-to-system capabilities, SAP and UL cover established PCN workflows, and consultants can retain spreadsheets or reproduce focused checks; no evidence shows a segment the entrant can dominate.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Winning the pre-release control point could plausibly extend into adjacent CLP, SDS, labeling, supplier-change, market-language, and other regulated release workflows across EU geographies. Those adjacencies are logical but unresearched, and each may add distinct regulatory, integration, localization, and liability burdens rather than becoming low-cost expansion.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Consultant-specific mappings, approved exceptions, and embedded approval history could create moderate switching costs, while an annual compatibility library can compound operational know-how. Public schemas and validation rules lower entry barriers, customer-controlled deployments fragment proprietary learning, and neither exclusive distribution nor a unique data asset is evidenced.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Local formula custody plus automated reconciliation across composition, UFI, SDS, labels, names, languages, and markets could improve privacy and error detection. The research provides no measured time saving, error reduction, release-capacity gain, security advantage, or comparison against ECHA, SAP, UL, and consultant-built processes, so behavior-changing superiority remains a hypothesis.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The harmonized obligation has applied since 2025, a 2026 pilot documented enforcement action and material non-notification, annual format changes sustain maintenance needs, and a limited distributor duty begins in 2027. Timing is favorable, though upstream coverage can eliminate many distributor cases and regulatory momentum also benefits incumbents.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Targeted outreach to a bounded set of specialist consultancies and a redacted or synthetic benchmark are feasible alongside employment, and a successful practice could expose the product to multiple clients. No consultant has committed, the payer-as-distributor arrangement may conflict with billable-service incentives, and every end-client deployment may introduce a separate security and integration sale.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data and automation background fits an initial exception-engine prototype, and consultant review avoids pretending software can supply regulated judgment. Production delivery still requires exact rule maintenance, qualified oversight, secure isolated deployments, annual regression, contractual liability controls, support across fragmented environments, and employer conflict clearance; the proposed capital and part-time workload are not validated against those demands.

main_structural_strength: The consultant-operated, customer-controlled architecture aligns a recurring mandatory release-control problem with domain-qualified review while avoiding a central vault of trade-secret formulations and potentially aggregating multiple SME clients through each practice.
primary_score_limiter: The consultant payer-and-distribution mechanism has no demand evidence, and its fragmented customer-controlled deployments may simultaneously weaken willingness to adopt, gross margin, scalable support, and the accumulation of a defensible shared data advantage.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: ECHA already provides free preparation, validation, multimarket, and system-to-system tooling, while SAP and UL document incumbent PCN/UFI workflows; this directly undermines any value proposition based mainly on dossier generation or submission access and leaves the claimed exception-control advantage unproved.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: At least two paid, independent consultant pilots using representative redacted or customer-controlled data, with pre/post measurements of reconciliation hours, defects caught, avoided rework, release throughput, deployment and support cost, security acceptance, renewal intent, and signed pricing that supports contribution margin after annual regression and qualified-review costs.
highest_value_structural_change: Standardize the fragmented deployment into a versioned local connector or appliance that keeps formulas in the customer environment but receives centrally maintained non-confidential rules and regression packs, then price the consultant on verified portfolio throughput or capacity gains; this would preserve custody separation while reducing per-client implementation cost and aligning payment with measurable consultant value.
